Three ways to hear the MSX

They are independent and can run at the same time. Two of them leave the cartridge as USB-MIDI and never pass through this server.

PSG raw — the square wave itself
The cartridge sends the PSG's fourteen registers down the serial link fifty times a second, and this page rebuilds the AY-3-8910 from them. The same sound as the machine's own chip, which is useful when that chip is dead. The synthesis happens in your browser, so the server needs no audio device and nothing has to be installed for it.
80%
buffered — frames 0 underruns 0
MIDI-PAC — PSG translated to MIDI
The cartridge watches the PSG and writes MIDI notes from what it sees. The timbre becomes a General MIDI instrument, so the square wave is gone. Works on any MSX, needs no support from the software running on it. Which instrument it becomes is your choice - the same GM number sounds different in every soundfont, and one that reads as a chiptune in one reads as a piano in another.
always on
MSX-MIDI — what the MSX itself sends
Software that drives the MSX-MIDI ports (MIDRY /I5 and the like) writes real MIDI; the cartridge passes it through untouched, so what you hear is what the composer wrote. There is nothing to switch — with no such software there is no traffic. While it is flowing, MIDI-PAC stays quiet so the two do not overlap. On an MSX without MSX-MIDI (HB-F1XD and the like) run PDMIDI once first, or the software reports “I/F not found”; an OCM needs nothing.

MIDI monitor

What the cartridge is sending as USB-MIDI — both paths above. They share one cable, and while MSX-MIDI is flowing the cartridge keeps MIDI-PAC quiet, so they never overlap. The browser reads the device directly, alongside whatever synthesiser is playing it.

MIDI monitor is off bars are octaves C1–C8, not audio

Hearing the two MIDI paths

They do not go through this server. The cartridge is a USB-MIDI device named PicoDock, so a synthesiser has to run on this computer. Most of them scan for inputs once, at startup.

General MIDI   fluidsynth -a coreaudio -m coremidi \
                          -o midi.autoconnect=1 font.sf2      (macOS)
               fluidsynth -a alsa -m alsa_seq font.sf2, then
                          aconnect PicoDock to it              (Linux)
               fluidsynth -a wasapi -m winmidi \
                          -o midi.autoconnect=1 font.sf2      (Windows)
               or Qsynth, the same with a window - see WINDOWS.md
               Soundfonts are a separate download.

MT-32/CM-32L   Munt (mt32emu). Needs the Roland ROMs, which are
               not distributed - dump your own hardware.

The MSX speaking

The host synthesises, the cartridge holds the samples, and the Z80 pours them into the PSG's volume registers — which become a DAC once the tone generators are switched off. Nothing is added to the machine. PDVOICE hello from DOS says it. Whether PDASK answers aloud is set on the Ask pane.

Voice — on
With this off the cartridge is told no, rather than left waiting for a sound that is not coming.
Monitor — hear it here too
Plays in this browser what the MSX is being sent, starting the moment the MSX starts playing it. The Sound pane's PSG raw cannot carry speech — it samples the registers fifty times a second and speech changes them ten thousand times — so it is hushed while the MSX talks, monitor on or not. This is what the MSX received; its speaker may still colour it.

Streaming hands the cartridge samples while the MSX plays, which means the Z80 reads the bus for every one of them — and that read is the only thing here whose timing is not ours. The other two put the whole utterance in the MSX's memory first and play from there, reading nothing while it sounds. They are slower to start and bounded by how much RAM is free, so the three are worth hearing against each other.

state idle rate — sent 0 played 0

The rate is measured, not assumed. How quickly the Z80 gets round its loop depends on how much of the bus the VDP is taking, and that differs from machine to machine — so the host watches how fast the cartridge's ring drains and synthesises the next sentence to match. The first one after a restart is a guess.

PicoDock server

The MSX sees a hard disk, a printer and a few extras that do not exist. This server is the other half of them: the cartridge asks over USB and the answers are made here, on this computer.

Nothing has to be configured. Start it, switch the MSX on, and the panes fill in as the MSX uses each thing.

The panes

DiskSectors as they are read and written.
FilesWhat is on the image now, and how to change it. Drop files on it to add them — on a folder to put them there. Tick entries and press Delete to remove them; tick exactly one for Rename. Delete stays greyed out while a ticked folder has anything in it, and says which one — a folder is only removed when it is empty, so one tick can never take a hundred files with it. Click a folder to work in it — the trail at the top left says where you are, and New file / New folder start there — and the In box in the dialog can be typed into, so somewhere you have not walked to works as well. Folders nest, so a folder inside a folder is fine. The triangle folds a folder without moving into it. Click a text file (.BAT, .TXT, .INI…) to edit it here — the line endings and the BASIC EOF byte are kept as they were. A file whose bytes cannot be reproduced exactly opens read-only, and so does one that is not text at all — a .BAS saved without ,A is tokenised, not text, however it is named. The list follows the MSX on its own; changes made from the host need Refresh. After any change, run PDSYNC on the MSX, or Nextor keeps showing the old directory.
PrinterPrint jobs, and where their bytes were kept. Pick one to read it; .txt / .png / .prn save it. Tick several and Make document merges them into one PDF — in the printer's own glyphs, or set again in a host font that is readable but loses the ESC/P layout. one page lays them end to end instead of giving each a sheet, so three short jobs take one sheet rather than three. Print… opens it in Preview so the system dialog picks the printer, copies and range. With --spool every byte lands in one file, so this is the way to get a job back out.
AskCALL PDASK("…") — what the MSX asked and what went back. A web search answers by default; switch to Me to type it yourself. You can still type one while the search is on, for when it brings back the wrong thing.
SoundThree ways to hear the machine, and how to switch them.
StatusWhat is true right now, rather than what happened.

Swapping files on the image

Pause the image first (Status pane), then mount it here. Pausing makes this server answer with an error rather than letting the MSX write underneath you. After a change, run PDSYNC on the MSX so MSX-DOS re-reads the directory.

When something looks wrong

No cartridgeUse a normal data cable, not a charge-only one. The Status pane says what it can see.
Enumerates, then disappearsTwo 5V supplies are fighting: the cartridge is powered by the MSX slot and by USB.
Printing hangsOn a 1chipMSX/OCM run PDFRCPRN once.
MIDI but no soundNothing on this computer is synthesising it. See the Sound pane.

On Linux, once

The port belongs to the dialout group, and ModemManager probes every new serial device to see whether it is a modem. Its probe holds the port, and it also raises DTR — which the cartridge reads as "the server is here", so Nextor can boot to <failed>.

sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER        then log out and back in
sudo cp 99-picodock.rules /etc/udev/rules.d/
sudo udevadm control --reload-rules && sudo udevadm trigger

The rule names only this cartridge, so ModemManager keeps running and your actual modems keep working. Replug afterwards.

This page

It is served on the loopback address only. It can pause your disk and switch cartridge features, so it is deliberately not reachable from the rest of the network.
